questions.q: What does Git track over the life of a project?
choices: Only the most recent version of each file
A complete history of changes as commits
Just the file names, not their contents
Only changes made by the project owner
questions.explanation: Git's core purpose is to record a complete history of changes as commits, letting you see what changed, when, and why — and roll back to any earlier state if something breaks.

questions.q: What is the main relationship between Git and GitHub?
choices: They are two names for the same tool
Git tracks history locally; GitHub hosts that history in the cloud for sharing
GitHub replaces the need for Git
Git only works inside GitHub Codespaces
questions.explanation: Git is a local version control tool that runs on your machine. GitHub is a hosting service that stores Git repositories in the cloud, making them shareable and accessible from anywhere. You can use Git without GitHub, but not the other way around.

questions.q: Cloud computing is best described as:
choices: Software that only runs on rainy days
A way of accessing computing resources on demand, without owning the hardware
A synonym for the internet in general
questions.explanation: Cloud computing means renting computing resources — servers, storage, databases — on demand over the internet, instead of buying and maintaining physical hardware yourself. You pay for what you use, and the provider handles the infrastructure.
